A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Wavy Transformer by the same authors. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, appendices, and checklists are readable and support matching retained content across renaming and reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original BERT pretraining and GLUE results, DeiT experiments, representation-similarity analyses, and throughput measurements, alongside some borrowed baseline scores.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds Light Wave results, sparse-graph evaluations, component ablations, computational measurements, and a causal-language-model experiment.

M1.justification: V2 retains the original architecture as Full Wave and introduces Light Wave, which removes the velocity FFN and normalization branches and uses a gated previous-layer momentum term (Section 5; Appendix B). Although v1 already discussed the momentum interpretation, this distinct implementation materially changes the block's computation.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained Wikipedia/BooksCorpus, GLUE, SQuAD-based analysis, and ImageNet coverage, v2 evaluates OGBN-Arxiv, OGBN-Proteins, Cora, Citeseer, and PubMed. Appendix A.5 also adds OpenWebText under causal attention, extending coverage to sparse-graph tasks and a distinct language-modeling scenario.

E2.justification: DIFFormer, previously only cited, becomes an evaluated diffusion baseline in the graph experiments. V2 also adds comparisons against CaiT-XXS-24 and a diffusion-only GPT-2 model under causal attention (Table 5; Appendix A.5), while retaining the BERT, DeiT, and FeatScale comparisons.

E3.justification: V2 reports a corrected GLUE evaluator and adds spectral-gap and variance diagnostics, graph depth and mixing-coefficient sweeps, a 150-epoch velocity-FFN ablation, and a specified 50-iteration causal fine-tuning protocol. The CaiT comparison omits class-attention blocks in the proposed model. Table 9's 100k-step convergence trajectory conflicts with the retained 10k-step description, so it does not establish that the original pretraining budget changed.

E4.justification: V2 adds MLM convergence analysis, spectral and feature-variance diagnostics, controlled removal of the velocity FFN, graph depth/mixing sensitivity tests, and layerwise representation-collapse analysis on Cora. These test convergence, component utility, and failure conditions beyond v1's retained cosine-similarity plots and partial-layer throughput analysis.

E5.justification: V1 already reports three-seed GLUE means and one-sigma similarity bands. V2 adds explicit three- and five-seed graph summaries, paired t-test significance indicators, and three-seed causal-loss averaging. The explicit GLUE three-seed statement disappears; the PDFs do not establish increased repetition of retained experiments.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises retained models' STS-B scores from 14.10/11.65/12.46 to 52.11/32.91/29.40 and changes their reported averages and ranking: Diffusion now exceeds Mix (+Full), while new Mix (+Light) leads at 66.12. These are revised evaluations, not demonstrated performance gains across versions. V2 also adds substantial Light Wave, CaiT, graph, diagnostic, convergence, cost, and causal-loss results; original Table 1 entries and Full Wave ImageNet accuracies remain.

T1.justification: V2 Appendix F replaces v1 Appendix E's faulty pairwise energy-dissipation derivation with the gradient-flow identity dU/dt = -||(I-A)X||², removing the erroneous one-half factor. Appendix B adds the Light Wave derivation with decoupled diffusion/wave step sizes. These are localized mathematical changes; the main energy theorems, symmetry assumptions, and Pre-LN analysis remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion extend the claimed empirical scope from NLP and CV to sparse-graph tasks. The central attention-as-diffusion interpretation, wave-based remedy, minimal-parameter claim, and no-extra-tuning claim remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: V1 presents the original mixed model as the best GLUE variant; v2 acknowledges Full Wave's overall underperformance after evaluator correction and favors Light Wave. New discussion distinguishes physical constraints from computational practicality, identifies graph settings where improvement fails or both models collapse, and explicitly limits conclusions from the short causal experiment, which shows no meaningful loss difference.

D1.justification: V2 announces a public code/model link, whereas v1 describes a reviewer archive and future public release. It adds Light Wave implementation guidance, graph gating initialization, diagnostic computation, causal fine-tuning settings, and training-time/memory measurements. Most original BERT and DeiT settings are relocated rather than changed; actual repository availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: New Section 4.2 distinguishes the work from physics-inspired sparse-graph methods, oversquashing research, and Hamiltonian-loss approaches. Added references include Deng, Gravina, Hamiltonian neural networks, OGB, nanoGPT, and CaiT. This refines positioning while retaining the original related-work framework and novelty argument.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the supplement into a consolidated experimental Appendix A, a Light Wave Appendix B, and relocated theoretical appendices. Main-text implementation sections move into the supplement, the experiments gain a model-variant overview and new subsections, and the GLUE and over-smoothing discussions are rewritten. Much of the introductory and methodological prose remains.

P2.justification: V2 adds extensive diagnostic, graph, convergence, ablation, deeper-model, and computational-cost tables, expands Tables 1–3 with Light Wave rows, and regroups Table 3 by backbone. The original five figures are retained with caption/legend refinements and relocation; existing implementation and throughput tables are moved and renumbered.

improvement.justification: V1 documents roughly halved DeiT throughput; v2 adds and measures a lightweight alternative near baseline throughput, alongside controlled component and robustness analyses that make effectiveness and failure conditions substantially more assessable. The corrected diffusion-energy derivation and acknowledgment of Full Wave's revised GLUE underperformance also strengthen reliability. Reporting weaknesses remain, including contradictory 10k/100k step labels and a 'few percent' memory claim despite 8.25 versus 9.14 GB for DeiT, but these do not outweigh the substantial methodological and evidential gains.
